en: Fragment of an unknown commentary on the *Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhi*, NAK 1-1679: vi. bauddhadarśana 31 = NGMPP B 23/7, single palm leaf;
also photographed by Tucci, perhaps by Daśabalaśrīmitra the Nepalese.
Arising from the wheel of the navel, shaken by the wind, radiant with the brilliance of a hundred lightning flashes,
having burnt the threefold enemies, honored by the three worlds, bathed in a stream of nectar,
possessing the essence of the flavor of Buddha-knowledge, stainless, she bestows a mass of bliss.
May Vārāhikā, who is devoid of the conceptualization of existence and non-existence, protect you!
I bow to that venerable, peaceful sage, auspicious in every respect,
by whose mere grace my own self-consecration became clearly manifest.
The secret means for the perfect accomplishment of the knowledge of reality is the union of the planes (*padamelaka*),
which is consumed according to one's own wisdom.
Whatever has been written by me, whether faulty or faultless,
the virtuous, who delight in the qualities of others, ought nevertheless to listen to it.

By this means, the desired state transmitted through the lineage of gurus is established; that very point of conjunction (lagna) is first indicated in the very first verse. Having kept this in mind, he speaks "Udyātā" and so forth, praising the Blessed Lady Kolāsyā by way of her manifestation throughout the world.

May Vārāhikā protect you—may she guard you. The root *pā* means "to protect. In the word *Vārāhikā*, the suffix *kan* is used in its own sense (as a nominalizer). She is called *Vārāhī* because she desires (*āhinoti*) or seeks (*ākāṅkṣati*) the *vāra*, which is the *samaya* (commitment) of *vajra*. *Vajra* is the *bodhicitta*; thus, she is so named because she seeks that commitment. The meaning is that she has the nature of innate bliss (*sahajānanda*). Of what nature is she? She is devoid of the investigation into existence and non-existence. "Existents" (*bhāva*) are trees, mountains, elephants, horses, and so forth—the portions of compassion in the form of conventional reality. "Non-existence" (*abhāva*) is their true nature (*svabhāva*), which is the non-erroneous reality.

The aspect of emptiness is by way of its manifestation. The investigation of those two is the determination of their essential nature; she is devoid of—that is, abandoned by—that [investigation]. What is meant by this? It means that her form is non-different from emptiness and compassion. Furthermore, of what nature is she? She is "risen," meaning emerged or arisen. From where? From the *talacakra*; a wheel situated on the base is a *talacakra*, namely the *nirmāṇacakra* (the emanation wheel). From that—furthermore, because it is below, it is "below" (*tira*). Again, she is "shaken by the wind"; *anila* is wind, meaning she is moved or impelled by it. Being impelled by the *apāna* wind, she is raised up; such is the sense.
Furthermore, she is radiant like a flash of lightning; etc., etc., etc.
